findings.title: API CORS reflects arbitrary origin with credentials
findings.description: The API reflects an untrusted Origin and allows credentials, so a malicious site could read authenticated API responses in a victim browser.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: Origin: https://doxa-cors-test.invalid -> Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://doxa-cors-test.invalid; Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true
findings.impact: A malicious website may be able to read responses from this application in a victim browser.
findings.remediation: Validate Origin against an explicit allow-list; never combine reflected origins with credentials.
findings.false_positive_notes: Impact depends on whether the endpoint returns authenticated, sensitive data.

findings.title: CORS reflects arbitrary origin with credentials

findings.title: Exposed Git repository metadata
findings.description: The .git directory is downloadable, allowing source code and history to be reconstructed.

cvss.justification: Repository metadata was confirmed readable without authentication; full source retrieval was not attempted, so confidentiality impact is scored Low.

findings.evidence: GET /.git/HEAD -> HTTP 200; content signature matched. ref: refs/heads/main
findings.impact: Sensitive configuration, source code or data may be disclosed to unauthenticated users, enabling follow-on attacks.
findings.remediation: Remove the file from the web root, deny access in the web-server configuration and rotate any credentials it contained.
findings.false_positive_notes: Signature matched file content. Confirm manually that this is not an intentional public file or a honeypot.

findings.title: Possible AWS access key ID in client-side code (app.js)
findings.description: 1 value(s) matching the pattern for AWS access key ID are present in JavaScript delivered to every visitor. DOXA did not use or validate the value.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence: AWS access key ID at byte offset 92 in app.js: 20 characters, sha256 prefix 457643f4 (value redacted)
findings.impact: Credentials or tokens embedded in client-side code are readable by every visitor and may allow access to backend or third-party services if they are valid.
findings.remediation: Remove secrets from client-side code, rotate any value that was real, and keep credentials on the server side. For public client keys, restrict them (referrer, scope, quota).
findings.false_positive_notes: Placeholders, public client-side identifiers (analytics or maps keys) and test fixtures often match these patterns. Verify manually whether the value is live and what it protects.

findings.title: Potential DOM-based XSS pattern: user-controllable sources and unsafe sinks (app.js)
findings.description: The script reads user-controllable values (location.hash ) and also uses unsafe DOM or code-evaluation sinks. DOXA did not trace the data flow, so this is an indicator only.

cvss.justification: Not scored: no directly demonstrated impact, or insufficient evidence for a defensible CVSS vector.

findings.evidence:
document.write(): 1 occurrence(s), first byte offsets: 674 
innerHTML/outerHTML assignment: 1 occurrence(s), first byte offsets: 730 
Sources present: location.hash
findings.impact: Unsafe DOM and code-evaluation patterns can turn attacker-controlled input into script execution (XSS) if the data flow is reachable. Manual review is required.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged locations. Avoid innerHTML/document.write/eval with untrusted data; use textContent or a sanitiser and add a Content-Security-Policy.
findings.false_positive_notes: Sources and sinks in one file are often unrelated. Confirm that attacker-controlled data actually reaches the sink.
